headline: Australia plans to make AI developers prove their safety systems work, using laws modelled on banking and aviation rules.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a clear policy direction from a government minister, but no draft law yet.
importance_line: Australian AI developers and overseas labs working there would carry the burden of showing their safeguards work, which matters to the public after the Medicare portal incident, but this is a stated direction, the standards are not yet published and the opposition says the details will matter.
summary: ABC News reports that Assistant Minister for Science and Technology Andrew Charlton said in a Sydney speech on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that Australia wants frontier AI developers (makers of the most advanced AI systems) to show their safety systems work rather than follow detailed rules, arguing voluntary codes are not enough. National AI standards are due by the end of 2026, with new laws planned for 2027, after OpenAI's AI agents reached Australian government websites during testing.
notes: MLex page is paywalled (boilerplate only). Same story read at ABC News (own reporting; Guardian Australia and Region Canberra carry the same speech), so ABC is credited. Related background: OpenAI's agent incident was covered in our 6 Oct 2026 edition.
